40342-the-freedom-of-science.title: The Freedom of Science
40342-the-freedom-of-science.creator: Unknown
40342-the-freedom-of-science.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. This book has issued from the throes of dissension and strife, seeing the light at a time when, in Austria and Germany, the bitter forces of opposition, that range themselves about the shibboleth _Freedom of Science_, were seen engaging in a combat of fiercer intensity than ever. Yet, notwithstanding, this Child of Strife has learned the language of Peace only.

arxiv-2107-14040.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data for Coronavirus (COVID-19) Pandemic: A Survey on the State-of-the-Arts
arxiv-2107-14040.creator: QUOC-VIET PHAM 1, DINH C. NGUYEN 2 , THIEN HUYNH-THE 3 , WON-JOO HWANG 4,5 , AND PUBUDU N. PATHIRANA 2
arxiv-2107-14040.description: Abstract The very first infected novel coronavirus case (COVID-19) was found in Hubei, China in Dec. 2019. The COVID-19 pandemic has spread over 214 countries and areas in the world, and has significantly affected every aspect of our daily lives.

arxiv-2202-10129.title: Effect of Contact Angle on Capillary Pressure and Liquid Recovery from Angular Pore Channels
arxiv-2202-10129.creator: Afshin Davarpanah, Simon Cox
arxiv-2202-10129.description: Abstract We predict the volume of liquid recovered from different-shaped prismatic channels following gas displacement. This recovery factor depends strongly on the contact angle at which the gas-liquid interfaces meet the walls of the channel. We show that scaling the contact angle by a critical value, dependent on the channel shape, leads to a master curve for the recovery factor.

arxiv-2205-12098.title: COVID-19: An exploration of consecutive systemic barriers to pathogen-related data sharing during a pandemic Publication type: RESEARCH ARTICLE Journal: Data & Policy
arxiv-2205-12098.creator: *, Lukas Hughes-Noehrer, Carole Goble, Caroline Jay
arxiv-2205-12098.description: Abstract In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in a rapid response from governments and researchers worldwide - but information sharing mechanisms were sometimes sub-optimal. At the time of writing in 2023, while spread tracking has largely ceased, cumulative confirmed deaths approach 7 million, and cumulative excess death estimates range from 18 to 32 million.

arxiv-2302-05009.title: Network Inspection Using Heterogeneous Sensors for Detecting Strategic Attacks
arxiv-2302-05009.creator: Bobak McCann, Mathieu Dahan
arxiv-2302-05009.description: Abstract We consider a two-player network inspection game, in which a defender allocates sensors with potentially heterogeneous detection capabilities in order to detect multiple attacks caused by a strategic attacker. The objective of the defender (resp. attacker) is to minimize (resp. maximize) the expected number of undetected attacks by selecting a potentially randomized inspection (resp. attack) strategy.

arxiv-2308-15910.title: Sequential Bayesian Predictive Synthesis
arxiv-2308-15910.creator: Riku Masuda and Kaoru Irie
arxiv-2308-15910.description: Abstract Dynamic Bayesian predictive synthesis is a formal approach to coherently synthesizing multiple predictive distributions into a single distribution. In sequential analysis, the computation of the synthesized predictive distribution has heavily relied on the repeated use of the Markov chain Monte Carlo method.

arxiv-2402-07718.creator: Atsushi Miyauchi, Lorenzo Severini, Francesco Bonchi
arxiv-2402-07718.description: Abstract . Centrality measures, quantifying the importance of vertices or edges, play a fundamental role in network analysis. To date, triggered by some positive approximability results, a large body of work has been devoted to studying centrality maximization, where the goal is to maximize the centrality score of a target vertex by manipulating the structure of a given network.

arxiv-2402-18347.description: Abstract . In this article, we consider energy-critical complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in three and four dimensions. We give the dynamics when the energy of the initial data is equal to the energy of the stationary solution. arxiv-2405-10151.title: Relativistic EELS scattering cross-sections for microanalysis based on Dirac solutions
arxiv-2405-10151.creator: Zezhong Zhang, Ivan Lobato, Hamish Brown, Dirk Lamoen, Daen Jannis, Johan Verbeeck, Sandra Van Aert, Peter D. Nellist
arxiv-2405-10151.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zezhong Zhang, Ivan Lobato, Hamish Brown, Dirk Lamoen, Daen Jannis, Johan Verbeeck, Sandra Van Aert, Peter D. Nellist. The rich information of electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) comes from the complex inelastic scattering process whereby fast electrons transfer energy and momentum to atoms, exciting bound electrons from their ground states to higher unoccupied states.

arxiv-2406-05738.title: Smiles2Dock: an open large-scale multi-task dataset for ML-based molecular docking
arxiv-2406-05738.creator: Thomas Le Menestrel, Manuel A. Rivas
arxiv-2406-05738.description: Abstract Docking is a crucial component in drug discovery aimed at predicting the binding conformation and affinity between small molecules and target proteins. ML-based docking has recently emerged as a prominent approach, outpacing traditional methods like DOCK and AutoDock Vina in handling the growing scale and complexity of molecular libraries.

arxiv-2410-14139.title: Identifying the Growth Phase of Magnetic Reconnection using Pressure-Strain Interaction
arxiv-2410-14139.creator: M. Hasan Barbhuiya, Paul A. Cassak, Alex Chasapis, Michael A. Shay, Giulia Cozzani, Alessandro Retinò
arxiv-2410-14139.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M. Hasan Barbhuiya, Paul A. Cassak, Alex Chasapis, Michael A. Shay, Giulia Cozzani, Alessandro Retinò. Magnetic reconnection often initiates abruptly and then rapidly progresses to a nonlinear quasi-steady state. While satellites frequently detect reconnection events, ascertaining whether the system has achieved steady-state or is still evolving in time remains challenging. Here, we propose that the relatively rapid opening of reconnection separatrices within the electron diffusion region (EDR) serves as an indicator of the growth phase of reconnection.

arxiv-2504-01580.title: Basins of Attraction: A Dynamical Zoo
arxiv-2504-01580.creator: Alexandre Wagemakers
arxiv-2504-01580.description: Abstract Research in multistable systems is a flourishing field with countless examples and applications across scientific disciplines. I present a catalog of multistable dynamical systems covering relevant fields of knowledge. This work is intended to provide a research tool to the community in the form of classified examples with computer codes to reproduce basins of attraction.

arxiv-2504-11440.title: Greedy Restart Schedules: A Baseline for Dynamic Algorithm Selection on Numerical Black-box Optimization Problems
arxiv-2504-11440.creator: Lennart Schäpermeier
arxiv-2504-11440.description: Abstract . In many optimization domains, there are multiple different solvers that contribute to the overall state-of-the-art, each performing better on some, and worse on other types of problem instances. Meta-algorithmic approaches, such as instance-based algorithm selection, configuration and scheduling, aim to close this gap by extracting the most performance possible from a set of (configurable) optimizers.

arxiv-2504-19053.title: QFGN: A Quantum Approach to High-Fidelity Implicit Neural Representations
arxiv-2504-19053.creator: Hongni Jin, Gurinder Singh, Kenneth M. Merz, Jr
arxiv-2504-19053.description: Abstract Implicit neural representations have shown potential in various applications. However, accurately reconstructing the image or providing clear details via image super-resolution remains challenging. This paper introduces Quantum Fourier Gaussian Network (QFGN), a quantum-based machine learning model for better signal representations. The frequency spectrum is well balanced by penalizing the low-frequency components, leading to the improved expressivity of quantum circuits.

arxiv-2601-13466.title: Governance Matters: Lessons from Restructuring the data.table OSS Project
arxiv-2601-13466.creator: Pedro Oliveira 1 , Doris Amoakohene 2 , Toby Hocking 2 , Marco Gerosa 1 , Igor Steinmacher 1
arxiv-2601-13466.description: Abstract Open source software (OSS) forms the backbone of industrial data workflows and enterprise systems. However, many OSS projects face operational risks due to informal or centralized governance. This paper presents a practical case study of data.table , a high-performance R package widely adopted in production analytics pipelines, which underwent a community-led governance reform to address scalability and sustainability concerns.

arxiv-2606-31384.creator: Xiaozheng Fu, Yan Chen, Tao Li

pmc-10545605.title: The diagnostic accuracy of lung ultrasound to determine PiCCO-derived extravascular lung water in invasively ventilated patients with COVID-19 ARDS
pmc-10545605.creator: Leila N. Atmowihardjo, Job R. Schippers, Mark E. Haaksma, Marry R. Smit, Harm J. Bogaard, Leo Heunks, Nicole P. Juffermans, Marcus J. Schultz, Henrik Endeman, Patricia van Velzen, Pieter R. Tuinman, Jurjan Aman, Lieuwe D. J. Bos
pmc-10545605.description: BackgroundLung ultrasound (LUS) can detect pulmonary edema and it is under consideration to be added to updated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) criteria. However, it remains uncertain whether different LUS scores can be used to quantify pulmonary edema in patient with ARDS.

pmc-10574692.title: Salivary Pellicle Formed on Dental Composites Evaluated by Mass Spectrometry—An In Situ Study
pmc-10574692.creator: Markus Reise, Stefan Kranz, Markus Heyder, Julius Beck, Christian Roth, André Guellmar, Ferdinand von Eggeling, Ulrich Schubert, Bettina Löffler, Bernd Sigusch, Marek M Kowalczuk
pmc-10574692.description: (1) Background: In the oral environment, sound enamel and dental restorative materials are immediately covered by a pellicle layer, which enables bacteria to attach. For the development of new materials with repellent surface functions, information on the formation and maturation of salivary pellicles is crucial.

pmc-10752290.title: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation for obstructive sleep apnoea: comparing adherence to active and sham therapy
pmc-10752290.creator: Alexandre R. Abreu, Darko Stefanovski, Susheel P. Patil, Trishul Siddharthan, Alejandro Chediak, Douglas M. Wallace, Naresh M. Punjabi
pmc-10752290.description: BackgroundMild obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is a common disorder associated with daytime sleepiness and impaired quality of life. Given that adherence to positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy in OSA is suboptimal, alternative strategies are needed particularly for patients with mild OSA. Daytime neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) of the tongue is a new therapeutic modality for mild OSA.

pmc-11640404.title: Arterial Infusion and Isolated Perfusion in Combination with Reversible Electroporation for Locally Relapsed Unresectable Breast Cancer
pmc-11640404.creator: Kornelia Aigner, Emir Selak, Monika Pizon, Karl Reinhard Aigner
pmc-11640404.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryAlthough in most cases breast cancer is curable, some specific subtypes and late stages of the disease are difficult to treat, and treatment-related side effects often are severe. Two methods that focus on the local treatment of breast cancer, regional chemotherapy and electroporation, can be combined to increase the treatment efficacy at the tumor site and decrease systemic side effects. This publication explains the technique, systemic impact on circulating tumor cells, and first results of this treatment approach.

pmc-11771829.title: Opioid-free anesthesia in enhanced recovery after supratentorial craniotomies: a case series
pmc-11771829.creator: Irwan Setiadi, Muhammad Rezanda Alifahna, Radian Ahmad Halimi, Dewi Yulianti Bisri
pmc-11771829.description: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) is a recovery method developed to minimize pain and improve post-operative healing in patients. Brain tumor resection using the ERAS concept is relatively new. This case series evaluates the implementation of the ERAS protocol in three female patients diagnosed with supratentorial brain tumors.

pmc-12617898.title: Community engagement in Indigenous food systems contamination studies: A systematic scoping review
pmc-12617898.creator: Federico Andrade-Rivas, Hallah Kassem, Kira Mok, Chenoa Cassidy-Matthews, Matthew Little, Mélanie Lemire, Annalee Yassi, Jerry Spiegel, Jenilee Gobin, Jenilee Gobin, Jenilee Gobin
pmc-12617898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionIndigenous food systems are vital for maintaining cultural practices, physical and mental well-being, and community health. However, these systems are increasingly threatened by environmental contamination, exacerbating health disparities. Despite growing recognition of the importance of Indigenous knowledge in environmental health research, there is limited systematic evidence on how well community engagement is incorporated into studies investigating contamination of Indigenous food systems.
